CIVN-2026-0568
**Multiple Vulnerabilities in Oracle Products**
Original Issue Date:November 20, 2026
Severity Rating: CRITICAL
Software Affected
- Oracle Database Server
- Oracle Application Express (APEX)
- Oracle Autonomous Health Framework
- Oracle REST Data Services
- Oracle Application Testing Suite
- Oracle Commerce
- Oracle Communications
- Oracle E-Business Suite
- Oracle Financial Services Applications
- Oracle Fusion Middleware
- Oracle Java SE and JavaFX
- Oracle MySQL
- Oracle GraalVM
For complete list of affected products refer to the oracle advisory:
[https://www.oracle.com/security-alerts/cspunov2026.html](https://www.oracle.com/security-alerts/cspunov2026.html)
Overview
Multiple vulnerabilities have been reported in various Oracle products which could allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code, gain elevated access, trigger denial of service condition and gain unauthorized access to sensitive information on the targeted system.
**Target Audience:** Individuals and organizations using the above-mentioned Oracle products.
**Risk Assessment:**
High risk of arbitrary code execution, unauthorized access, denial of service, information disclosure and privilege escalation.
**Impact Assessment:**
Potential for unauthorized access to sensitive information, denial of service, privilege escalation and full system compromise.
Description
Oracle products are used for several applications including enterprise-level data management, cloud solutions, software development, and business applications. They are employed across a wide range of sectors, including finance, healthcare, manufacturing, government, and retail, among others.
Multiple vulnerabilities have been reported in Oracle products including Helidon, JD Edwards EnterpriseOne Localizations, MySQL, Oracle Access Manager, Oracle Database Server, Oracle E-Business Suite, Oracle Java SE, Oracle WebLogic Server, and others due to improper input validation, access control weakness, and other security weaknesses. A remote attacker could exploit these vulnerabilities by sending a specially crafted request to the targeted system.





Successful exploitation of these vulnerabilities could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary code, elevate privileges, obtain/disclose sensitive information, bypass security restrictions, cause memory corruption, cause denial of service (DoS) conditions, gain unauthorized access, access restricted files or directories, manipulate application data, and achieve compromise of affected systems on the targeted system.
For complete list of affected products, CVEs, workarounds and solutions, refer to the Oracle security updates:
[https://www.oracle.com/security-alerts/cspunov2026.html](https://www.oracle.com/security-alerts/cspunov2026.html)
Solution
Apply the security updates released by Oracle:


[https://www.oracle.com/security-alerts/cspunov2026.html](https://www.oracle.com/security-alerts/cspunov2026.html)
